entries.mechanism: PolicyEngine UK's carers_allowance formula treats carers_allowance_reported > 0 as an eligibility trigger and pays the statutory weekly rate (86.45 * 52 = 4495.40) with no minimum-age condition, so it awards Carer's Allowance to child-aged Enhanced FRS records (all 152 mismatching persons are aged 0-15, each carrying a reported CA amount of 4004.71 that the survey attributes to a child record). The Axiom RuleSpec applies the statutory 16-or-over gate (SSCBA 1992 s.70(3)), so entitled_to_carers_allowance is false and the annual amount is 0. Axiom is statutorily correct; PolicyEngine overpays by omitting the age condition. Filed upstream as PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#1793. The residual equals the full statutory annual award PolicyEngine pays.

Carer Support Payment (the Scottish Carer's Allowance replacement from 2025) has the same mechanism as Carer's Allowance: PolicyEngine UK pays the statutory weekly rate (98.15 * 52 = 5103.80) on reported carer receipt with no minimum-age gate, awarding CSP to child-aged records (all 12 mismatching persons are aged 0-15). The Axiom RuleSpec applies the statutory 16-or-over gate (Carer's Assistance (Carer Support Payment) (Scotland) Regs 2023, reg. 5), returning 0. Axiom is correct; PolicyEngine overpays. Filed upstream as PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#1793.

PolicyEngine UK's dla_m pays the higher-rate mobility component (80.00/week) from the frozen dla_m_category FRS input with no minimum-age condition. All 34 mismatching children are aged 0-2 yet carry dla_m_category = HIGHER. Statute (SSCBA 1992 s.73(1); the higher-rate mobility age floor is 3, lowered from 5 by the Welfare Reform and Pensions Act 1999 from April 2001) bars the higher-rate mobility component below age 3. The Axiom RuleSpec gates on child_is_aged_3_or_over, returning 0. Axiom is correct; PolicyEngine pays a component the child cannot legally receive. Filed upstream as PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#1793. The residual is the full weekly higher-rate mobility amount.

The annual child DLA residual is exactly the higher-rate mobility component (80.00/week) annualised. Both engines agree on the highest self-care component (114.60/week * 52 = 5959.20, the Axiom value); PolicyEngine additionally pays higher-rate mobility (80.00/week) to the same 34 children aged 0-2, giving 194.60/week * 52 = 10119.20. The Axiom RuleSpec omits the mobility component because those children are under 3 (SSCBA 1992 s.73(1)), so its annual amount is 5959.20. Same PolicyEngine age-gate omission as the weekly mobility entry; filed upstream as PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#1793.
